Subject: Pilot ask & onboarding concession - healthcare pilot

Hey Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Aurelia is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed. We have internal pressure to keep pilot economics tight while we validate clinical throughput. Two asks from procurement:

1) A substantive onboarding credit for the first 3 months (they're looking for 30-35% of estimated pilot spend).
2) A firm onramp commitment: if we guarantee $150k committed spend in the first 6 months, can we secure preferential per-token rates for the pilot and a capped price for year 1?

We'd like to avoid a long legal negotiation — procurement suggested we put something with your sales leader and finance for a quick alignment and then wrap in the MAP.

Attached a short mutual action plan and estimated usage table.

Sara

Head of Clinical AI Programs | Aurelia Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-27T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot ask & onboarding concession - request for pricing path + CFO signoff

Marissa / Marcus — forwarding Aurelia's ask. Short ask from me: they want a 30-35% onboarding credit + preferential pilot rates if they commit $150k over 6 months. They are strategic in laterally aggregated hospital networks and could expand to enterprise in 12 months.

Why I think we should consider a concession:
- High expansion upside (their internal roadmap maps to ~1.2M ARR if pilot validates)
- Pilot volume is bursty but predictable by day-of-week; our runtime efficiency should keep effective unit costs lower than competitors

Proposal for internal approval (split-commitment structure):
- Commitment: $150k committed spend over first 6 months.
- Upfront concession: 20% onboarding credit applied to first invoice (not refundable).
- Volume discount: additional 10% on spend above the committed amount during months 1-6 (so effective max onboarding + overage reduction ~30%).
- Term: 12 months minimum; if they sign 18 months and hit $250k ARR target in year 2, we accelerate margin rebate of additional 5%.

Business impact (ballpark):
- Revenue recognized (first 6 months): gross billable $150k, net to Redwood after credits ~120k; incremental capacity cost estimate ~35k -> gross margin preserved at ~50% with these concessions.

Ask: need Marcus/Ben signoff for a 20% onboarding credit + ability to structure a second-stage rebate contingent on expansion (Ben/CFO for final). If we can't do 20%, what's the max we can offer without further exec signoff?

I'm attaching the quick pricing scenarios. Happy to hop on a 20-min call.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Storefront_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

Dylan — thanks for the clear ask and the scenarios. Two comments from GTM:

1) We want to protect net revenue for Q1. A 20% onboarding credit is plausible but I would cap total startup concessions at 25% (onboarding + one-time credits).
2) We need legal to review the expansion-trigger language — prefer a clear metric for the "accelerate margin rebate" (e.g., 250k ARR sustained for 2 consecutive months).

Marcus — can you confirm margin impact if we do 20% onboarding + 10% overage discount? Please include the cash collection timing assumption (we cannot allow a concession that delays cash >45 days).

If Marcus green-lights, Ben will need a short memo to sign off. Dylan, can you draft a one-page exec memo that spells out the ask, revenue tradeoffs, and expansion probability? I can include a GTM note on upsell cadence.

-Marissa

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 09:10 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus — can you confirm margin impact if we do 20% onboarding + 10% overage discount?

Quick finance take: I ran Redwood_Storefront_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx with conservative usage and payment timing assumptions. Key outputs:
- If we do 20% onboarding credit + 10% overage discount, the first-6-months net cash to Redwood (assuming 30-day invoicing) is ~$118k on $150k gross billings.
- Estimated incremental infra/runtime cost: ~$36k over 6 months.
- Resulting gross margin ~45% (below our target but within acceptable corridor if we treat this as a strategic incubator).

Stretch concession we can approve now (finance + revenue ops):
- Approve a 20% onboarding credit now without Ben's signature, provided the contract term is >=18 months OR the customer pre-pays 50% of the committed $150k within 30 days.

We should escalate to Ben for anything beyond 20% onboarding credit or above 2-tiered rebate structures. I can draft the short cost memo for Ben.

-Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive memo: Aurelia Health pilot concession request (CFO approval needed)

Ben — looping you in for final approval. Below is the executive summary that I will append to the contract and send to Aurelia pending signoff. I have attached the one-page memo as PDF for quick review.

Executive summary:
- Customer: Aurelia Health (regional hospital system; pilot across 3 hospitals)
- Ask: 30% equivalent onboarding concession on estimated pilot spend + preferential pilot rates for $150k committed spend in first 6 months.
- Our recommended structure (Sales + Finance): 20% onboarding credit applied at first invoice + 10% overage discount on spend above committed amount during months 1-6. Contract term: 18 months OR pre-payment of 50% of committed amount within 30 days. Contingent rebate: additional 5% rebate if customer hits $250k ARR within 12 months.
- Financials (conservative): first-6-months net cash ~118k; incremental infra cost ~36k; gross margin ~45%. Upside: probability-weighted expansion to 1.2M ARR over 24 months.
- Risk mitigations: require pre-pay OR 18-month term; cap total one-time concessions at 25%; include clawback language for early termination.
- Requested approval: Ben, approve a one-time onboarding concession of 20% and authority to sign the split-commitment structure. If you want to authorize a 25% cap (onboarding + credits) we can close faster at a slightly higher revenue cost.
